- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward; delay downward adjustment until 2–3 days after peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75% of recent high), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.
- In low-sentiment periods (e.g., sentiment <0.05), model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for suppressed volatility.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day high, reduce by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or negative; otherwise, maintain unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of true price decline.
